sbh2.4:1.2: The fivefold *-mātra* (mere) sequence is the structural core: mere formation, mere dharma, mere substance, mere cause, mere effect. *Mātra* functions as a reductive operator — there is *only* the conditioned arising, no extra entity (doer, owner, agent).
sbh2.4:1.4: *dharmāṇām eva dharma-āhārakatvam* — 'the carrying of dharmas by dharmas alone.' Phenomena produce phenomena, with no third entity (a self, an agent, a soul) involved. A precise Yogācāra formulation of *anātman* in causation.
sbh2.4:1.5: *niṣkāraka-vedakatvam* — 'the absence of an agent or experiencer.' *Kāraka* is the grammatical-philosophical term for the agent of an action; *vedaka* is the experiencer of feeling. The action happens; the experience happens; but no one is doing or undergoing.
sbh2.4:2.1: *Mohādhikaḥ ... moha-caritaḥ* is kept as delusion-predominant and delusion-conduct, matching the conduct-label style in the surrounding practice chapters. Two verbs are paired: *prajahāti* (abandons) followed by *tanū-karoti* (makes thin). Compare *maitrī*'s *pratanu-karoti* alone. The doubled action against *moha* suggests stronger or two-staged work: abandoning in the moment of recognition, then thinning the underlying tendency over time.
